thread:
maria: Hey, spotted a sharp latency/throughput regression on node pool us-west-2-gpu-b around 12:03 UTC, looks correlated with a scheduler change rolled ~12:00. 99p token latency up from ~45ms to ~210ms.
sam: ugh, saw alerts too. dashboards show kv prefix-hit-rate collapsed from ~82% to ~6% in about 90s.
ryan: any deploy in that window? deploy-bot: deploy started by anya at 11:59:45 UTC: rollout/scheduler-adjust-allow-prefetch-v2 -> prod.
anya: I rolled a small change to the scheduler to allow speculative prefetching on idle workers to improve cold-starts. can revert if that's the culprit.
maria: profiling shows a lot more get_prefetch() traffic and many small one-off prefix loads that are displacing long-lived prefix hot entries. Eviction logs: `kv_cache.evict_count=1.2M` during the spike.
sam: logs snippet from one runtime: ```WARN kv_cache: prefix eviction triggered, shard=13, reason=burst_prefetch, victim_prefix=tenant_42_longprefix, current_hitrate=0.05```
ryan: kernel selection note: during the same timeframe we started falling back to generic_gemm kernel for many smaller batches. perf profile: CPU stalls up, GPU utilization oddly unchanged. Could be eviction causing more CPU-side serialization.
maria: hypothesis: speculative prefetching created thundering small-key loads across shards -> cache churn -> kernel heuristics see different sequence length distribution -> pick less-optimal kernels -> latency spike.
anya: config excerpt I pushed: ```yaml
scheduler:
  speculative_prefetch: true
  prefetch_window_ms: 30
  prefetch_limit_per_sec: 10000
```
sam: interesting: prefetch_limit_per_sec looks high. For tenant-heavy traffic that could generate >10k small prefixes/sec.
ryan: I ran a local repro by toggling prefetch. With prefetch=false the prefix-hitrate stayed ~80% and kernel selection stayed on fused_fp16 for majority batches. With prefetch=true it dropped and generic_gemm increased 3x.
maria: we have a noisy-tenant signature: many short, highly unique prefixes at 1-2 token length which are exactly what prefetch grabs. Those are polluting the LRU.
anya: rolling back now to speculative_prefetch=false on prod rollback-176855-revert. deploy-bot: rollback started at 12:15:10 UTC.
sam: immediate telemetry after rollback: within ~45s eviction rate drops, prefix-hitrate climbs back to ~78%. 99p latency trending down toward baseline.
ryan: follow-up items I propose: 1) add tenant-aware prefetch throttles 2) change prefetch to prefer local shard-hot prefixes 3) telemetry hook to flag prefetch-caused eviction storms 4) update kernel heuristic to consider recent cache-hit distribution when picking kernel.
maria: also add a canary gate: speculative_prefetch only enabled on canary pool for 24h and requires hit-rate delta < 5% for 10m.
anya: sorry for the disruption, I didn't anticipate churn. Will open PR for the canary gating and throttle changes.
sam: quick mitigation: add immediate rule to block prefetch for tenants with >200k unique prefixes in 5m. That should stop noisy tenants from poisoning global LRU.
ryan: I'll create a perf dashboard showing kernel-selection transitions + prefix-hitrate side-by-side so it's easier to correlate next time.
maria: Thanks. Note for postmortem: cause = speculative prefetch enabled globally -> generated thundering small-key prefetches -> KV cache eviction storm -> altered batch/seq distribution -> kernel selection fallback -> 99p latency spike. Mitigations listed above.
anya: PR: https://rb.redwood.dev/PR/1234 will include throttles + canary gating.
sam: leaving this thread open for any extra logs. I pushed an automated alert rule to notify if prefix-hitrate delta > 30% within 2m when any scheduler flags change.
ryan: added a short script to dump kernel-selection histogram for a pod: `kubectl exec -it pod -- /usr/local/bin/dump_kernel_hist.sh` — put that in runbook.
maria: ok closing after rollback validation at 12:32 UTC. If anyone sees recurrence re-open. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: rollback completed successfully at 12:18:04 UTC (rollback-176855-revert).
